questions.q: Which of these counts toward a model's context window?
options: Only the exact text the user just typed
The system prompt, conversation history, tool results, and the new message — all together
Only the model's training data
Only text written in English
questions.explain: The context window is a shared token budget covering everything sent in a request: system prompt, history, tool outputs, attachments, and the new message.

questions.q: As verified in this lesson against provider documentation, what is Claude Haiku 4.5's context window?
options: 1,000,000 tokens
4,000 tokens
200,000 tokens
500,000 tokens
questions.explain: Claude Haiku 4.5, Anthropic's fastest tier, has a 200,000 token context window, smaller than the 1,000,000-token window of the Opus/Sonnet/Fable flagship tier.

questions.q: What happens when a request exceeds a model's context window?
options: The model silently drops the oldest text and continues
The model automatically summarizes the overflow
The request fails with an explicit error — the application must manage trimming itself
The context window automatically doubles
questions.explain: Exceeding the context window causes the request to fail outright; it's the calling application's responsibility to trim, summarize, or retrieve only relevant content.

questions.q: Why isn't a larger context window automatically a complete solution for working with long documents?
options: Larger context windows are always slower to download
Context windows cannot contain more than one document
Larger context windows never support system prompts
Models can underweight information buried in the middle of a very long context ("lost in the middle")
questions.explain: A bigger window raises the token ceiling but doesn't guarantee the model attends equally to everything inside it — information in the middle can get less attention than content near the start or end.

questions.q: What pattern lets an application work with a document far larger than the model's context window?
options: Retrieving only the most relevant chunks of the document instead of sending the whole thing (RAG)
Converting the document into an image before sending it
Ignoring the context window limit entirely
Always switching to the smallest available model
questions.explain: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) embeds a knowledge base and retrieves only the most relevant chunks at query time, letting an application work with sources far larger than any single context window.
